note: Original factual annotations. Event URLs cite dates and claims; coordinates locate the named place approximately, not battlefield boundaries. BC dates use astronomical years (1 BC = 0).

items.title: Shared government
items.text: Diocletian established the Tetrarchy in AD 293. Split locates his later palace, not the exact place this arrangement was proclaimed.

items.title: Constantinople
items.text: Constantine founded his new capital at Byzantium in AD 330.

items.title: Western court
items.text: After Theodosius died in AD 395, his sons ruled western and eastern portions. Rome is a western urban anchor, not a claim that it was the sole court residence.

items.title: Eastern court
items.text: Arcadius ruled in the East after Theodosius’s death.

items.title: Ravenna
items.text: Ravenna became the seat of the Western Roman Empire in AD 402.
items.source: UNESCO, Early Christian Monuments of Ravenna
